Ants emerged from the fallen rainforest trunk, carrying pale fragments through a landscape thoroughly rearranged by the downpour.
Children excavated ambitious tunnels; teenagers arranged themselves around a speaker; older swimmers stood waist-deep, discussing something with great seriousness.
Outside the snowbound village shop, a handwritten notice offered deliveries to neighbours unable to reach the newly cleared path.
Above this practical business, the lanterns swayed with a slower rhythm, their reflections slipping across glazed bowls and the polished backs of wooden toys.
Behind the glass, damp had softened the corners of a timetable until the paper curled away from its frame.
Beneath this watchful gathering, a fisher counted the catch, his pencil moving steadily across a damp sheet of paper.
Under the midday sun, the dunes had lost the long shadows that explained their shapes.
A groundskeeper pushed his mower beneath trees already beginning to undo his work, dropping another leaf behind him every few steps.
My uncle crossed the room to close the curtains, and the simple movement restored a little privacy against the enormous weather outside.
Coral ridges appeared close enough to touch, although whole schools of fish passed between them and my drifting shadow.
A shop assistant tucked the final corner beneath a ribbon, briefly transforming somebody's hurried purchase into an object that appeared carefully considered.
The river curved behind the barn and spread into a shallow bend where cattle stood drinking among the reeds.
Nervous supporters repeatedly stood and sat, making a restless pattern that travelled through the stadium before the match began.
At the reference table, a student worked through a problem, covering the margin with increasingly impatient figures.
Each jolt tilted his head towards his neighbour, who quietly shifted to let him rest.
Bulbs chased one another around painted signs; a mechanical dragon swung between floodlit clouds of steam.
Dawn arrived unevenly across the farmyard, touching the upper windows before it reached the muddy ground.
I watched it struggle free, carrying a dusting of pollen away beneath this enormous, briefly flowering world.
A cleaner guided a mop around occupied chairs, apologising softly whenever someone moved their feet.
Outside, rain travelled almost horizontally across the bay, erasing the far cliffs until the world seemed to end at the nearest broken rock.
The ruined castle enclosed wet grass and a wooden bench where a crowded great hall had once demanded attention.
Above the locked gate, a plastic ribbon fluttered, continuing some small celebration after its audience had gone.
Nobody spoke much, yet the small room felt companionable, as though waiting out the weather were a shared occupation.
A sudden shower of crystals marked the passage of a squirrel; then the canopy was still again.
Customers negotiated the food stalls with bowls held carefully level, knowing one careless elbow could turn supper into a public spectacle.
Closer, the dry season had left its marks everywhere: split earth, brittle stems, a water hole reduced to a dark oval.
At a shuttered shop, a child studied her reflection in the glass while her parents argued softly over boarding passes.
Lanes that had felt endless were merely painted strips; the deep end was an exposed slope scattered with leaves.
Beyond the last bend, the passage opened onto water so still that the cave seemed to continue downwards forever.
On a doorstep worn hollow by generations, a woman was polishing the same small brass plate.
Her correction was so quick that the production line appeared never to have needed her.
A late arrival negotiated a row of knees; a child investigated the velvet armrest with solemn attention.
Above her, relatives disputed the correct amount of spice with the affectionate certainty of people who had conducted this argument for years.
Cloud shadows travelled down the mountains and drifted across the lake, turning the water from green to almost black.
The hills we had planned to climb were finally visible beneath a clean blue sky.
In the centre of the gallery stood a marble dancer, caught forever in the instant before a leap.
The uneven notes climbed through the warm air, giving this immense view the unexpected intimacy of a room next door.
Children searched the tideline for useful rope, and from the schoolhouse came the scrape of chairs being dragged into the sun.
When the owner called out an offer of tea, his voice seemed to come from another century.
For a moment, all three stood listening, their elaborate costumes rustling whenever they took a breath.
The smell of fried onions travelled from a stall lit by a camping lamp, drawing a small, patient crowd.
Bubbles hung beneath it in long, uneven necklaces, and the reeds cast shadows so faint they seemed unfinished.
A heavy-smelling flower drove me towards another greenhouse bed, where tiny blossoms released a sharp and startling scent of lemon.
At regular intervals, the beam revealed a wedge of empty sea, then surrendered it to the night again.
Shattered windscreens glittered among dull panels, and a line of washing machines faced west like spectators waiting for a show.
Through an open doorway, I glimpsed a family clearing supper from a table fitted around a living trunk.
At the edge, a boy rehearsed a movement with his hands, explaining a trick to his sister while she studied the slope.
Behind me, the station continued its modest routines: a printer chattering, someone searching for a missing pen.
Rain had washed soil into the escalators, where ferns now climbed in orderly green ranks.
Only after several minutes did I notice the sand shifting, grain by grain, beneath a half-buried ray.
Through the spray, I could make out a strip of beach and, beyond it, cliffs rising like broken teeth.
Glass birds fluttered inside their cages, embroidered rivers rippled across folded cloth, and a stallholder weighed somebody's dream on brass scales.
On every screen, the same message appeared, addressed to a crew who had not yet been born.
I pressed my palm against the nearest patch of wallpaper and felt warmth, then movement.
Rainwater had gathered in the hollows of the carved saints, giving their worn faces the appearance of grief.
Dust softened every surface in the study except the upper edge of the empty picture frame.
Through the narrow window in the door, the suspect watched a cleaner mop muddy footprints from the corridor, one by one.
Every passing bus briefly hid the man at the opposite end, yet he was always closer when it cleared.
Somewhere in the darkness, a mule complained with a voice more homesick than his own.
I remember almost nothing of the meal, only the warmth of the plate and our gradually shrinking silences.
Behind it followed the manager, holding a croissant with the strained optimism of a man attempting a diplomatic negotiation.
Her childhood bedroom had become the place where unwanted things waited: a broken lamp, spare blankets, a printer nobody could persuade to work.
Visitors followed arrows between beds of identical flowers while speakers offered advice on healthy thoughts.
Each winter, a ruby appeared outside the kingdom's poorest house, warm enough to clear a small circle in the snow.
A man's blue shirt turned behind a round window, lifting one sleeve as if making a slow, uncertain greeting.
By morning it had gone, leaving shells in the umbrella stand and her late husband's footprints beside the bed.
Bicycle chains hung where tickets had once been sold, and seedlings filled a popcorn machine.
Along its creases, buses balanced like insects, while commuters squeezed between the teeth of a silver zip.
Unable to refuse them, her father arranged the white roses in every vase he could find.
From the ridge, it looked temporary: a scattering of pale boards set against the enormous patience of the land.
Only a waterfall, briefly silver in the evening sun, marked an opening in the rock.
I kept my hands in my pockets, and even the shadows here seemed eager to slip away from their owners.
Cups waited beside the abandoned ship's dark screens while a forgotten jacket still hung over the captain's empty chair.
The corridor seemed longer on the return journey, and doors I had counted before were missing, their numbers faintly visible on unbroken plaster.
A bell sounded somewhere within the ruined abbey, although its tower stood open to the sky.
A pale rectangle marked the study wall beneath an empty frame, yet no broken glass disturbed the dust below.
Beside the recorder lay the stolen watch, its delicate gold strap absurdly bright against the scratched surface.
Anna's phone showed one per cent battery, and behind her, the gate she had just crossed swung shut with a metallic snap.
Beyond the ditch, the British hills dissolved into rain, and Lucius crouched beside a smoky fire, turning his sandals towards its uncertain warmth.
Whenever she leaned forward to protect it, her hand came close to mine, and below, the harbour darkened from blue to ink.
The hotel's breakfast room promised elegance, and silver spoons gleamed on spotless cloths; a pianist murmured something expensive in the corner.
Yet the pencil marks recording her height remained beside the door, and she traced the highest line with her thumb.
Someone had placed a security cone around it, and two gardeners waited nearby, consulting the regulations before deciding what to do.
High on the mountain, the greedy mayor waited in borrowed rags for a miracle that visited only the poorest households.
Beside me, an elderly woman folded a child's jumper across her knees, and she smoothed it twice, although it needed neither fold nor smoothing.
Each August, the sea slipped beneath my aunt's door carrying salt, small fish and a few apparently embarrassed crabs.
The cinema still advertised a film that nobody alive remembered seeing, and beneath the torn poster, our settlement's repair shop occupied the old foyer.
Somewhere inside the paper, a woman was ironing a thunderstorm, and with each stroke, the sky above her became a little smoother.
In her bedroom, the dress still hung beneath its thin cover, one sleeve extended slightly, as though she had been interrupted while reaching for something.
Wind pushed dust through the unfinished church, gathering it in the corners where pews would eventually stand.
While the rope bridge trembles above the river's muddy racing water, the far bank promises shelter beneath its densely crowded trees.
Tiny blue lights drift above the enchanted garden's flowers, while a child receives one trembling light inside an ordinary drinking glass.
Driverless buses glide between towers above the city's crowded streets; guidance lights stitch precise blue routes between the transparent towers.
A pale hand presses against the outside of my bedroom window as rain follows its fingers down towards the unreachable street below.
While rain streaks the windows above the mansion's deserted entrance hall, a mourning dress retains its solitary vigil beside the cold hearth.
Three cups occupy a table set with only two chairs, while one porcelain rim retains a warmth the empty house cannot explain.
Police lights sweep across the bank's shattered entrance windows; an evidence bag gives ordinary coins an unfamiliar ceremonial importance.
The unlit car remains opposite our door after midnight as its driver watches the entrance with an attention that excludes everything else.
Horses drag laden carts along the town's deeply rutted street as women exchange the morning's news while waiting beside the communal well.
Her scarlet scarf rests beside mine across the small café table, while our hands hesitate together around the offered cups of coffee.
The dog wears a hat that completely conceals its ears; its owner conducts an increasingly indignant search around the living room.
My childhood shoes stand beside their larger replacements near the door as their disproportion makes pride and grief briefly difficult to separate.
While identical houses line the street beneath slowly turning surveillance cameras, each arriving child becomes the camera's brief and involuntary centre.
A tiny cottage glows beside the forest's cold black edge, while its enchanted oven recognises courtesy more reliably than any royal seal.
His worn coat hangs beside mine behind the kitchen door; one missing button recalls a morning I had considered quite ordinary.
My grandmother's cups sing softly when she pours their morning tea as my grandmother listens while continuing to butter the morning bread.
While grass covers the road between shops abandoned many years earlier, goats occupy the classroom with complete indifference to its former purpose.
The moon proceeds along the street wearing my father's oversized shoes, while a fish requests bread by ringing the baker's completely ordinary bell.
His clean red boots wait beside the garden's closed back door; the abandoned swing describes no further journeys above the uncut grass.
Dust sweeps past the frontier town's wooden bank and shuttered saloon as a tethered horse shifts beneath a sign complaining on its hinges.
Beyond the final settlement beneath the steep mountain slopes, a narrow track commits itself to the rising weather.
Beneath an ancient tree beyond the village's outer gardens, a cobbler repairs shoes whose golden soles have never touched earth.
Behind the observation glass on the spacecraft's silent upper deck, two moons assemble an unfamiliar dawn above an unnamed continent.
Beneath the bed inside a room I locked myself, another breathing rhythm begins precisely where my own deliberately ends.
Beneath the ruined tower beyond the ancestral house's neglected gardens, white roses obscure a name the stone can scarcely preserve.
Beneath the open window beside the garden's rainless gravel path, wet footprints commence without any corresponding approach across the dry ground.
Inside an interview room beyond the police station's reception desk, a recovered watch gleams beside coffee abandoned during an abrupt confession.
At the far end of the station's deserted midnight platform, a solitary figure reproduces each of my movements with deliberate precision.
Beneath smoking lamps inside the printer's cramped upstairs workshop, an apprentice assembles tomorrow's news from reversed fragments of metal.
Beneath the garden's oldest tree beyond the crowded afternoon party, he has arranged two chairs around the book I thought lost.
Beneath the mayor's portrait inside the town hall's crowded reception, a misplaced umbrella transforms the mayor's nose into a dripping beak.
Inside my childhood bedroom at the end of summer, the toy cars reveal how quietly my own scale has changed.
Beneath the public screen above the town's regulated central garden, citizens arrange their expressions in accordance with the morning instructions.
Beneath the bridge beyond the king's carefully guarded pleasure gardens, a frog wears the lost crown with suspiciously practised dignity.
At a bus stop outside the shuttered neighbourhood florist, a woman steadies her shopping as though it contains something fragile.
Beside the washing machine inside our otherwise ordinary family kitchen, a small raincloud awaits its customary release through the back door.
Inside the ruined cinema beyond the town's collapsed river crossing, rows of beans climb towards light once excluded for the audience.
Beneath my bed beside a box of discarded school exercise books, a miniature sky assembles clouds from misplaced household objects.
On the table beside the breakfast she will never finish, a lipstick mark survives the warmth that once gave it meaning.
Beside the river beyond the plain's long dry approach, a rider counts cattle against the last copper light of evening.
While our boat scrapes the rocks below the island's shadowed cliff, a cave mouth holds a light nobody expected to find.
The white horse crosses the lake without disturbing its surface, while silver fish escort its passage beneath the transparent evening water.
The service robot navigates the lunar kitchen with a tray; its illuminated eyes register a cup with almost personal satisfaction.
The dolls face the doorway before my hand reaches the latch as one porcelain mouth appears to be attempting a difficult smile.
While the ancestor's portrait hangs above the library's permanently locked door, one pale finger indicates the garden's least frequently visited corner.
Dust covers every frame except one beside the study door, while a pale square records the recent removal of something carefully concealed.
The shop's rear door stands open above rain-darkened concrete steps; oily tracks continue towards a street the rain has almost washed clean.
My phone illuminates the room with an unexpected incoming photograph as its subject is myself in the position I still occupy.
While steam spreads across the platform beneath the approaching locomotive's whistle, a returning soldier lifts his sister above the confusion of greetings.
She laughs at the flour dusting my face and sleeves, while the space between our shoulders becomes unexpectedly difficult to ignore.
The king's oversized robe trails behind him like a carpet; a mouse occupies the crown with substantially greater confidence.
My father asks my opinion without offering his own first as the kitchen's unchanged furniture suddenly contains an unfamiliar version of me.
While mechanical birds gather above the gates with red recording eyes, their wings issue small metallic acknowledgements whenever somebody speaks a name.
Golden apples burden the poor woman's otherwise unremarkable garden tree, while each hungry visitor departs with more than the woman keeps herself.
The emptied flat returns each footstep with an unfamiliar brightness; pale rectangles retain the shapes of pictures already travelling elsewhere.
Snow falls from the postman's coat onto our sun-warmed summer doorstep as my mother provides the towel she always keeps for his visits.
While abandoned towers rise beyond the city's increasingly dense fringe of trees, a washing line abruptly contradicts the apparent completeness of the abandonment.
The staircase plays a tune whenever I approach the landing, while a door listens with an ear too large for its frame.
White roses crowd the room beneath the untouched wedding dress; her father supplies fresh water as though care could alter timing.
The railway station stands alone beyond miles of windswept prairie grass as a locomotive announces its approach with a slender distant plume.
While the final customers drift towards the darkening market entrance, a vendor gathers the evening into folds of faded cloth.
Thin smoke curls above the snowbound courtyard roofs, while a cyclist dislodges frost that glitters briefly against grey brick.
Traffic gathers in restless queues around the crowded junction; pedestrians thread the stationary vehicles with the precision of needles.
Muddy floodwater creeps along the submerged residential street as a plastic chair navigates the drowned road with absurd dignity.
While silver fish gleam beneath the market's harsh electric lamps, a stallholder sluices yesterday's traces towards the gurgling drain.
A patient queue curls around the brightly advertised windows, while shoppers rehearse their purchases with lists clenched like boarding passes.
Fresh snow settles along the park's deserted wooden benches; a child receives the falling flakes with astonished open palms.
Scarlet fireworks blossom above the city's crowded winter rooftops as a child's delighted laughter survives the thunder of another burst.
While candlelight returns familiar faces to the suddenly darkened street, neighbours gather chairs into an improvised circle of conversation.
Our footsteps echo between rows of sleeping concrete pillars, while a green exit sign offers a small island of certainty.
Two petrol pumps glow beside the otherwise deserted highway; the surrounding landscape absorbs the light without revealing its edges.
Idle yellow machines fill the fenced construction site's corners as a departing worker sheds the day's weight in flakes of mud.
While heat shimmers above the stationary cars along the road, a passenger's dog surveys the impasse with extravagant interest.
Clouds of steam billow from the round metal steamer, while a vendor folds warm parcels into the shelter of paper bags.
Pink reflections ripple across the rain-polished surface of the street; pedestrians navigate the broken colours beneath their dark umbrellas.
A solitary bus idles beneath the station's tired yellow lamps as its driver prolongs a cup of tea beside the shuttered office.
While empty swings trace slow arcs through the cooling evening air, a mother's final call draws the last boy towards home.
Traffic threads the streets far below the crane's narrow cabin, while the city's immense buildings shrink to carefully arranged geometric blocks.
Gulls wheel above the dump's uneven mountain of discarded things; a shredded shopping bag struggles against the fence like trapped seaweed.
Drums thunder beneath a procession of brightly fluttering flags as children answer with paper flowers trembling above their heads.
While rainwater ticks from the bamboo's slender leaves around us, the enclosed stillness lends each falling drop an improbable clarity.
Rosy dawn spreads across the lake's unbroken sheet of ice, while an imprisoned branch remains suspended beneath the crystalline surface.
Torchlight picks out wet leaves above the night-darkened path; an unseen chorus fills the canopy with relentless metallic rhythms.
The asphalt runs towards hills blurred by rising heat as its distant surface shimmers with the promise of nonexistent water.
While palms cluster around the oasis's small pool of clear water, a thirsty bird punctures the pool's bright stillness with its beak.
White water plunges between the gorge's steep dark walls, while its unbroken roar leaves almost no room for human speech.
Clouds conceal the valleys far below our narrow summit; distant peaks resemble islands whose shores remain permanently out of reach.
Terraced paddies catch the sunset in narrow bands of red as a farmer descends the embankments with the patience of long familiarity.
While mist conceals the hilltops beyond rows of dark tea bushes, the clipped bushes retain their orderly lines beneath the drifting veil.
The wind tugs fiercely at coats along the cliff path, while waves detonate far below against the coastline's jagged dark defences.
Storm-torn seaweed marks the beach in uneven brown ribbons; a splintered branch shares the sand with an immaculate blue bucket.
Striped fish weave between coral branches above the pale sand as sunlight redraws its restless lattice across the patches of bare sand.
While wisps of mist drift above the jungle river's brown surface, an unseen bird sends one clear note through the canopy.
A single torch picks out rough stone inside the cave, while the remaining darkness seems to gather just beyond its reach.
Steep limestone towers rise above the river's slow grey current; our passing boat disturbs their reflections more than the surrounding air.
Charred trees stand above the forest's pale carpet of ash as a single green shoot makes the surrounding devastation newly visible.
While ripe apples weigh down branches above the orchard's wet grass, a picker tests each apple with an almost conversational touch.
Leaf shadows tremble across the narrow lane's sun-warmed surface, while a wren investigates the gaps in a wall mottled with lichen.
Wind-driven sand sweeps between the town's rapidly shuttering houses; residents vanish indoors with their faces hidden in hastily lifted scarves.
Sunflowers lower their heavy heads above the heat-baked field as the passing wind offers movement without the smallest promise of relief.
While a weary mother tucks a coat around her sleeping child, the clock maintains a precision nobody finds remotely comforting.
Students spill along the corridor with bags and unfinished goodbyes, while a paper aeroplane sails magnificently above the departing backpacks.
Moonlight lays a pale rectangle across the empty classroom floor; a forgotten coat preserves the outline of an absent child.
Chairs scrape across the floor as conversations cross the classroom, while a pencil drums an insistent accompaniment against a scarred desktop.
While open textbooks occupy every available corner of the library tables, students measure their progress in emptied bottles and exhausted sighs.
Battered books lean together along the shop's crowded wooden shelves, while a sleeping cat claims an unsorted carton with complete authority.
Old trunks crowd the attic beneath its low sloping roof; a broken rocking horse waits among objects nobody can quite discard.
My grandmother turns festival cakes in a heavy black pan as their sweetness travels through the kitchen before the first serving.
While pans hiss across the crowded kitchen's line of glowing burners, the head chef's clipped instructions cut through the competing metallic sounds.
Fresh loaves crowd the shelves behind the bakery's darkened window, while another tray enters the oven through a brief furnace-coloured opening.
Blue shirts revolve behind the laundrette's brightly lit round windows; a waiting customer folds warm towels with deliberate almost tender care.
Dark hair scatters across the floor beneath the barber's chair as clipped hair gathers into a dark provisional shadow beneath the chair.
While a small clock marks the silence above the dentist's door, a child follows the aquarium's fish with fiercely concentrated attention.
The final lamp illuminates the museum's enormous weathered stone lion, while a cleaner's bucket introduces a temporary note of practical brightness.
Green foam spills over the beaker onto the laboratory bench; the teacher restores order with instructions sharper than the children's laughter.
The blank screen glows above the cinema's slowly filling seats as the rustle of popcorn establishes the audience's first collective soundtrack.
While the lift judders to a halt between two unmarked floors, its emergency button offers a red assurance the passengers examine closely.
Enormous brass wheels revolve inside the tower's dim stone chamber, while each deliberate tick sends a faint tremor through the floorboards.
Green birds flutter between perches behind the crowded shop window; a rabbit contributes only the faintest rhythm of unhurried chewing.
Examination desks replace the sports hall's familiar open playing space as an oversized clock presides above the rows with uncompromising visibility.
While airport lights gleam across the polished floor beside our luggage, a sleeping child manufactures darkness beneath the shelter of a coat.
Passengers crowd beneath a departure board whose times keep changing, while each revised arrival time releases another small wave of disbelief.
Fields flash past the high-speed train in bright uneven strips; a farmhouse appears only long enough to suggest an entire life.
The sleeper carriage rocks above the steady rhythm of wheels as one reading lamp preserves a private island of unfinished wakefulness.
While grey waves strike the ferry beneath its shuddering passenger lounge, unattended cups attempt small escapes across the polished tabletops.
Our cable car glides above the valley's steep green sides, while the river below contracts into a bright almost decorative thread.
Commuters ascend in close rows above the station's continuous rumble; their shoulders brush without quite interrupting the privacy of their thoughts.
The canal boat glides past gardens behind the sleeping houses as one kitchen window contributes a square of domestic gold.
While fruit-laden boats gather beneath houses raised above the muddy water, a purchase crosses the water with one practised outstretched arm.
Container ships wait beside towering stacks of red and blue cargo, while cranes lean over the vessels with the measured patience of wading birds.
Dawn brushes the fishing boats moored along the wet harbour wall; a fisher draws another length of net from a tangled heap.
Waves batter the lighthouse beneath its steadily revolving yellow beam as the rotating beam briefly exposes a sea apparently determined to climb.
While empty deckchairs wait behind the pier's locked winter gates, a torn café sign applauds the wind with solitary irregular claps.
Snow smothers the hut beneath the blizzard's steadily rising voice, while the occupants draw closer as the landscape disappears beyond the glass.
Students sing as the school coach climbs the winding hill; a teacher guards the register with the air of protecting evidence.
Festival lanterns glow above the temple's wide open doors as incense threads their quiet procession with a fragrance older than memory.
While bright fabric links the village houses above the wedding guests, neighbours supply additional chairs with the assurance of accustomed cooperation.
White flowers droop above the banquet's abandoned plates and glasses, while a cleaner gathers the discarded ribbons into a surprisingly small bundle.
Paper cups litter the steps beneath the stadium's empty tiers; a solitary cleaner gathers the crowd into rustling heaps of paper.
Collapsed tents dot the field beyond the abandoned festival stage as crows inspect the wreckage with the patience of professional scavengers.
While holiday crowds cover the beach in overlapping towels and umbrellas, children negotiate its temporary frontiers with dripping buckets and absolute confidence.
Skaters circle beneath the ice rink's cool blue lighting, while a beginner negotiates the wall with fierce and unsmiling determination.
The alarm sounds above the fire station's wide red doors; boots strike the floor in a brief accelerating percussion.
Overheated pupils queue beside the sports field's bright running lanes as teachers shelter their clipboards beneath hats with improbably generous brims.
While red bowls crowd the table between dishes releasing fragrant steam, additional chairs enter the room like relatives nobody expected to miss.
Bright flowers crowd buckets along the festival market's narrow street, while customers lower their faces towards blooms as though listening for advice.
Children whisper behind the curtain in their borrowed concert costumes; one young performer examines his hat as though it contains the answer.
Lanterns glow above the festival crowd like a second sky as parents lift their children into a less obstructed share of wonder.
While snow covers the seats of the abandoned fairground's rusting wheel, a carousel horse keeps its painted gaze fixed beyond the gates.
Weeds spread across the deserted theme park's once crowded paths, while a grinning dragon offers an increasingly unconvincing welcome above the gate.
Ruined castle walls rise above the restless dark coastal water; seabirds enter windows from which human observers have long disappeared.
Mist drifts between weathered gravestones above the long wet grass as a rook maintains its solitary watch above the rusting entrance gate.
While fallen leaves gather beneath the empty pool's faded diving board, each passing gust adds another leaf to the unofficial collection.
Dust blankets the furniture beneath the abandoned house's fractured ceiling, while a sapling claims the staircase with the confidence of rightful ownership.
Small fish drift through the wreck's shattered bridge windows; sand settles over cups arranged for a voyage that never finished.
Pipes crowd the submarine's low ceiling above its narrow passage as a crew member turns sideways between bunks and suspended clothing.
While snow obscures the windows of the isolated polar research base, a single lamp gathers the team's abandoned boots into domestic order.
Earth rotates beneath the station's window in blue and white, while clouds drift over continents with an indifference that seems almost instructive.
Enormous leaves overlap above the greenhouse's narrow rain-darkened walkway; disturbed leaves release stored water onto the visitors moving below.
Along the path, new channels carried red soil towards the stream, and I paused beside a fallen trunk.
Every approaching wave briefly reorganised the shoreline, sending shoes, towels and half-built castles into the hands of people who had only just settled down.
The school was a difficult expedition; the next valley might have belonged to another country.
Under the lanterns, colours became difficult to trust, and a blue scarf looked purple until the stallholder held it beneath his white lamp.
Somewhere above, nesting birds moved beneath the roof, making small repairs to a building nobody else appeared to need.
Fishing boats lit the harbour before sunrise, their deck lamps revealing glistening nets and the restless backs of the catch.
Beside the vehicle, a discarded strip of metal was too bright to examine, and I narrowed my eyes towards the horizon.
In the sun, office workers loosened their scarves; in the shade, the benches held a damp chill.
Beyond it waited tall cupboards, faded portraits and the uncertain shapes of covered furniture, and my uncle crossed the room to close the curtains.
Beneath a coral ledge, a patterned creature turned and vanished against the rock with the precision of a changing illusion.
Beneath the glittering holiday decorations, exhausted shoppers drifted between queues like travellers searching for a route home.
I followed the current with my eyes until it disappeared behind willows, leaving only their trembling leaves to suggest the water's continued passage.
Below the stands, a goalkeeper adjusted his gloves with exaggerated care, and around me, supporters kept standing, then sitting again.
Snow melted from abandoned gloves on a radiator, and damp footprints faded between the shelves.
Elbows fitted between bags; shoulders supported strangers through the bends, and an announcement crackled overhead, its useful words swallowed by static.
Bulbs chased one another around painted signs; a mechanical dragon swung between floodlit clouds of steam, and in the gaps between attractions, darkness returned abruptly.
Beyond their small urgency, cattle stood breathing clouds into the cold, waiting with the immense patience of creatures whose breakfast followed a dependable routine.
Daffodils stood openly in the sun; pale buds remained tightly folded along the shaded wall.
At the far end, a family shared a packet of biscuits with exaggerated politeness, and each opening of the corridor door interrupted them.
With each wave, the coastline disappeared and reassembled itself, and black ledges vanished beneath a boiling rush of foam, then emerged streaming and unchanged.
Even in ruin, the building could still determine how much of the world you saw.
The playground preserved the afternoon in scattered fragments: a chalk score, a crushed juice carton, the dusty outline of a shoe across the climbing wall.
Rain softened the afternoon street into blurred watercolours while the café windows glowed with the reassuring warmth of lamps.
I listened to the silence after our footsteps stopped, and far away, a branch cracked with the clean sharpness of breaking china.
Under the bare bulbs, steam wrapped each cook in a shifting veil scented with ginger and sizzling garlic.
When a breeze finally moved through the grass, the whole plain whispered with the same dry, papery voice.
Midnight had thinned the crowds without dimming the departure hall's relentless brightness, and cleaning machines hummed between islands of luggage.
On the far wall, a painted dolphin continued its leap above water that was no longer there.
Our lamps exposed a narrow shelf along its edge; beyond that, the lake absorbed their light.
Iron ties held the canal's oldest walls together while cracks travelled between windows overlooking the more flexible reflections below.
Between these mechanical patterns, workers communicated through raised eyebrows and practised gestures, and one woman caught a crooked label before it reached the scanner.
Gilded figures leaned from the theatre's balconies as the orchestra settled on a single note and conversation gradually loosened.
Steam clouded the windows; flour settled on shoulders; warm air escaped whenever somebody opened the back door.
Beyond that small, precise effort, the mountains rose in immense layers, their upper slopes already losing the afternoon light.
Families stepped between them carrying damp bedding and expressions of determined cheerfulness, and at our feet, a drowned map spread its colours into the mud.
A guard began closing the shutters, removing the afternoon from one window at a time.
At street level, the city had felt crowded and impatient, and from the roof, its movement appeared almost graceful.
Along the shore, exposed roots gripped the air where sand had disappeared, yet the morning was astonishingly clear.
To reach the history shelves, I had to turn sideways beside a leaning stack of atlases.
Under the bulbs, their painted smiles appeared unusually fixed, and somebody's phone vibrated among the hairpins; nobody reached for it.
With the traffic lights dead, the junction acquired a hesitant courtesy, and drivers edged forward, paused, exchanged gestures through open windows.
Somewhere within the frozen surface, a deep note sounded, then travelled away beneath the snow.
In the far corner, a flower the colour of raw meat leaned over the path.
Climbing the spiral staircase, I felt the tower receive each wave through its stone foundations.
Beyond the fence, new houses stood in careful rows, their windows reflecting the same copper sky as the ruined cars.
Built into the forks of enormous trees, the settlement adjusted itself to the forest's movement.
From the highest ramp, the skatepark resembled a shallow grey sea, its waves fixed in concrete.
The observation deck faced the planet's night side, and below, lightning spread through enormous cloud systems, briefly exposing patterns no map recorded.
Rain had washed soil into the escalators, where ferns now climbed in orderly green ranks, and the fountain supported a small pond, busy with insects.
Above us, a pump started with a shudder, sending ripples across my tea, and the station's instruments tracked currents and temperatures continuously.
Beneath the ruined gateway beyond the deserted desert settlement, fresh hoofprints establish the first dependable direction we have seen.
Behind the concealed doorway within the village baker's shop, a staircase ascends through clouds towards an impossibly green moon.
Beneath the orbital city's crowded network of artificial streets, vast machines sustain the atmosphere with a reassuringly unvarying rhythm.
Behind the closed door beyond the house's unlit corridor, my mother's voice rehearses sentences she never lived to learn.
